acceptance: `evolve inbox withdraw <id> <reason>` removes a pending unclaimed item and records a `withdraw` ledger line (red: no such subcommand)
A claimed, routed or consumed item is refused and left untouched (exit 1)
After a withdrawal, `evolve inbox add` files the same id again
fix: Add `evolve inbox withdraw <id> <reason>`: remove a pending, unclaimed root item that no cycle has claimed or routed, append a `withdraw` ledger line with the reason, and refuse a claimed, routed or retired item (exit 1). A withdrawn id may be filed again.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: `evolve inbox add` files an item and appends a `file` ledger line, but the only verb that removes an item is `evolve inbox consume`, which retires its id for good. An item filed with a mistake (the wrong scope, a better-specified re-filing) is therefore deleted by hand, leaving two `file` ledger lines for one id and no record of the withdrawal. Found by the architecture re-review of `evolve inbox add` (2026-09-30).
title: No verb withdraws a just-filed inbox item, so a mistaken filing is deleted by hand and the ledger records two filings
